Tips to avoid common SEO Execution Mistakes
Some of the main SEO Mistakes I see people do when developing processes are:

* Just following checklists and best practices without prioritizing SEO activities to what will actually drive business and achieve goals in a cost effective way. It's fundamental to understand websites' business goals (and what decision makers are looking to achieve) and tie your SEO goals and activities to them.
* Just doing or not doing something because X or Y big competitor is, without taking your own context, goals and challenges into account.
* Targeting queries due to high search volume and overall relevance without considering the role within the customer journey.
* Overlooking branded queries (yours and your competitors).
* Working SEO on a silo without taking into account key areas / departments initiatives.

Underestimating the budget allocation required for SEO ROI, and similarly, not allocating the correct resources to support the SEO strategy.

Relying too much on tools to dictate their work instead of critical thinking and applying their knowledge of the business and users.
Natasha Burtenshaw-deVries
X Linkedin Threads
One common SEO mistake I often see is an over-reliance on short-term results rather than building a long-term strategy. Many businesses focus heavily on quick wins, such as keyword stuffing or excessive link building, instead of prioritizing valuable content and user experience that naturally attract and retain traffic. Additionally, ignoring technical SEO elements such as site speed and mobile optimization can severely impact rankings, even with the best content. Lastly, failing to adapt to algorithm updates and relying on outdated tactics can hinder growth.
Rohit Kurup
X Linkedin Threads
A common mistake is believing that ad hoc auditing and fixing items flagged from external tools is enough to 'tick over' SEO. And tied to this, the sentiment that SEO can be completed with ad hoc projects.

SEO has to be an always-on part of marketing activities. It can be vastly underappreciated as the channel to make everything work harder toward your business goals and steer (through data) impactful marketing decisions for ongoing growth.
Lee Wilson
X Linkedin Threads
Failing to understand the intent of the targeted keywords. For example, targeting a high search volume keyword with informative intent on a catalog page.

Forgetting the impact other channels could have on SEO and how SEO can feed into other channels with data sharing and strategy alignment.

Analyzing the traffic of a website without considering external factors like, for instance, seasonalities or breaking events or economy evolution of the targeted market. Pruning some content just because it doesn’t work for SEO, but it does it great for other channels
